text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Two Queen's Counsel with formidable reputations will be in action in the court case starting today between Workers' Party chief J.B. Jeyaretnam and 11 leaders of the ruling People's Action Party.
- The Government has set aside S$50 million over the next five years to reimburse public hospitals which give research time off to their doctors, says Health Minister Mr Yeo Cheow Tong.

- With more than a quarter of Singapore legislators newly elected, and half of the Indonesian parliament also taking their seats for the first time in October, the new members of the two legislatures must meet and maintain the close rapport of their leaders, says Singapore Speaker Tan Soo Khoon.
- The first car cooperative was launched at Toh Yi estate with a slew of penalties aimed at the inconsiderate user.
- DBS Land deputy chairman Han Cheng Fond says the Singapore private housing market is nowhere near collapse but agrees that there could be a mismatch between potential supply and demand.

- Sembawang Corp has appealed to the Ministry of National Development to revise its zoning blueprint for Sembawang so it can redevelop its 82-hectare shipyard and industrial site at Admiralty road into a waterfront township.

- The Shangri-La Asia hospitality group is selling a second stake of new shares to Singapore Government-owned Temasek Holdings, this time raising HK$774 million as the Singapore company takes an increasingly active investment profile in Hongkong.
- Stock markets worldwide kick off this week to a jangling uncertainty over whether last Friday's 3.1 percent sell-off of U.S. stocks is the start of a tailspin that pulls down other markets with it.
- The property market is not headed for a collapse, in the view of DBS Land deputy chairman Han Cheng Fong.
- A senior Chinese official issued a sharp warning to currency speculators that China would use its massive foreign exchange reserves to defend the Hong Kong dollar if necessary.
- DBS Land announced a 12.8 percent rise in group net earnings to S$113.46 million at half-time.
